name: Red Team
summary: Offensive tooling for authorized penetration tests and red-team engagements
description: Credential attacks, exploitation helpers, Active Directory and Windows protocol tooling, and pivoting utilities for engagements you have written authorization to perform. Several cornerstone frameworks (Metasploit, Responder, NetExec, BloodHound, Sliver) are not in Debian main and are listed as external tools with vendor install instructions rather than bundled.

tools.name: THC-IPv6
tools.summary: Toolkit for attacking and testing IPv6 and ICMPv6
tools.notes: Ships many separate programs named atk6-* (e.g. atk6-alive6, atk6-parasite6); see the package's file list for the full set.

tools.name: Weevely
tools.summary: Generate and manage a stealthy PHP web shell

tools.name: CeWL
tools.summary: Build a target-specific wordlist by spidering a website

tools.name: crunch
tools.summary: Generate wordlists from a character set and pattern

tools.name: CUPP
tools.summary: Build targeted password dictionaries from personal data

tools.name: hashcat
tools.summary: GPU-accelerated password recovery for a wide range of hashes
tools.notes: GPU acceleration needs the appropriate OpenCL driver for your hardware; without it hashcat falls back to the CPU.

tools.name: hashID
tools.summary: Identify the type of a given password hash

tools.name: THC Hydra
tools.summary: Parallelised network login brute-forcer for many protocols

tools.name: John the Ripper
tools.summary: Offline password hash cracker with many formats

tools.name: Medusa
tools.summary: Parallel, modular login brute-forcer for network services

tools.name: Ncrack
tools.summary: High-speed network authentication cracking tool from the Nmap project

tools.name: Ophcrack
tools.summary: Crack Windows LM/NTLM passwords using rainbow tables
tools.notes: Rainbow tables are downloaded separately; the package ships the cracker, not the tables.

tools.name: Patator
tools.summary: Multi-purpose brute-forcer with fine-grained control

tools.name: FreeRDP
tools.summary: Remote Desktop Protocol client for reaching Windows hosts

tools.name: iodine
tools.summary: Tunnel IPv4 traffic through a DNS server to bypass filtering

tools.name: Kerberos clients
tools.summary: MIT Kerberos tools (kinit, klist) for AD ticket handling

tools.name: polenum
tools.summary: Retrieve the password policy from a Windows host over SMB

tools.name: ProxyChains-NG
tools.summary: Force a program's connections through a chain of proxies

tools.name: Impacket
tools.summary: Python classes and example scripts for Windows network protocols
tools.notes: Ships many impacket-* example scripts (secretsdump, wmiexec, psexec, GetUserSPNs and more); the command shown is one of them.

tools.name: ldapdomaindump
tools.summary: Dump Active Directory information over LDAP into readable reports

tools.name: smbclient
tools.summary: Command-line client for SMB/CIFS file and print shares
tools.notes: The smbclient package also ships rpcclient and nmblookup, handy for Windows/Samba enumeration over MS-RPC and NetBIOS.

tools.name: smbmap
tools.summary: Enumerate SMB shares and permissions across a network

tools.name: sshuttle
tools.summary: Transparent proxy and VPN over an SSH connection for pivoting

tools.name: Aircrack-ng
tools.summary: Suite for monitoring and testing Wi-Fi (WEP/WPA) security
tools.notes: Monitor-mode capture needs a wireless adapter and driver that support it.

tools.name: Bully
tools.summary: Brute-force Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) PINs

tools.name: hcxdumptool
tools.summary: Capture WPA key material from Wi-Fi devices for offline cracking

tools.name: hcxtools
tools.summary: Convert Wi-Fi captures into hashcat and John formats

tools.name: hostapd
tools.summary: Access-point and authentication daemon for rogue-AP testing

tools.name: iw
tools.summary: Configure Linux wireless devices and monitor mode

tools.name: MDK3
tools.summary: Wi-Fi stress testing and deauthentication (802.11)

tools.name: MDK4
tools.summary: Wi-Fi stress testing and attacks (802.11), MDK3 successor

tools.name: Pixiewps
tools.summary: Offline WPS PIN recovery (pixie-dust attack)

tools.name: Reaver
tools.summary: Brute-force Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS) PINs

tools.name: rfkill
tools.summary: Enable and disable wireless (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) radios

tools.name: wavemon
tools.summary: Ncurses monitor for wireless signal and link quality

tools.name: Wifite
tools.summary: Automate wireless auditing using the aircrack-ng tools

tools.name: Wireless Tools
tools.summary: Classic iwconfig/iwlist utilities for wireless interfaces

external.name: Metasploit Framework
external.summary: Widely used exploitation and payload development framework
external.license: BSD-3-Clause for the framework; the Rapid7 installer and some content have their own terms.

why.text: The framework is not packaged in Debian; Rapid7 ships its own cross-distribution installer and nightly builds and expects to be updated from there.

how.text: Install the official omnibus package or nightly build from Rapid7's documented instructions for Linux, then update with msfupdate.

external.name: NetExec
external.summary: Network execution and enumeration across SMB, WinRM, LDAP and more
external.license: BSD-2-Clause (open source), successor to CrackMapExec; not packaged in Debian.

why.text: NetExec is maintained outside Debian and changes rapidly; upstream recommends installing it with pipx into an isolated environment.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx (pipx is in Debian): pipx install git+https://github.com/Pennyw0rth/NetExec.

external.name: Evil-WinRM
external.summary: WinRM shell for authenticated access to Windows hosts
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source), distributed as a Ruby gem; not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Evil-WinRM is published as a Ruby gem and is not packaged in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install the gem with 'gem install evil-winrm' (Ruby is in Debian), or run it from the official git checkout.

external.name: Responder
external.summary: LLMNR, NBT-NS and MDNS poisoner for credential capture
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source), not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Responder is free software but is not in Debian; it runs directly from a git checkout with Python 3.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run Responder.py; it uses only the Python 3 standard library.

external.name: BloodHound
external.summary: Graph-based Active Directory attack-path analysis
external.license: Apache-2.0 (Community Edition) with a separate commercial Enterprise edition.

why.text: BloodHound Community Edition ships as container images and release bundles outside Debian; collectors are distributed with it.

how.text: Run BloodHound Community Edition from the official Docker Compose deployment, and collect data with SharpHound or BloodHound.py.

external.name: Sliver
external.summary: Cross-platform adversary-emulation and command-and-control framework
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source), not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Sliver is released as prebuilt binaries by Bishop Fox and is not packaged in Debian.

how.text: Download the official server and client release binaries for Linux from the Sliver releases page and verify their signatures.

external.name: Exploit-DB (searchsploit)
external.summary: Local copy of the Exploit Database with the searchsploit CLI
external.license: GPL-2.0 for the tooling; exploit entries carry their own terms. Not in Debian.

why.text: The exploitdb archive and its searchsploit client are maintained by OffSec outside Debian.

how.text: Clone the official exploitdb repository and link searchsploit onto PATH; update with 'searchsploit -u'.

external.name: RouterSploit
external.summary: Exploitation framework for embedded and router devices
external.license: BSD-3-Clause (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: RouterSploit is a Python framework on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx, or run from the official git checkout.

external.name: pwncat
external.summary: Post-exploitation platform and upgraded reverse-shell handler
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: pwncat is published on PyPI/GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install pwncat-cs').

external.name: Ropper
external.summary: Display information about and find ROP gadgets in binaries
external.license: BSD-3-Clause (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Ropper is published on PyPI and is not in Debian trixie (ROPgadget, which is, covers similar ground).

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install ropper').

external.name: enum4linux-ng
external.summary: Enumerate Windows and Samba hosts over SMB/RPC
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: enum4linux-ng is a Python rewrite on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx, or run from the official git checkout; it uses the Samba client tools.

external.name: CrackMapExec
external.summary: Swiss-army knife for assessing Active Directory networks
external.license: BSD-2-Clause (open source); not in Debian. Succeeded by NetExec.

why.text: CrackMapExec is unmaintained in favour of NetExec and is not in Debian; prefer NetExec.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx, or use its successor NetExec.

external.name: Certipy
external.summary: Enumerate and abuse Active Directory Certificate Services
external.license: MIT (open source); not in Debian (Debian's 'certipy' is an unrelated tool).

why.text: The AD-CS tool Certipy is on PyPI/GitHub and is not in Debian; Debian's python3-certipy is a different certificate utility.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install certipy-ad').

external.name: Kerbrute
external.summary: Brute-force and enumerate Active Directory accounts via Kerberos
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Kerbrute is a Go tool distributed as release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture, or build with 'go install' (Go is in Debian).

external.name: PingCastle
external.summary: Audit the security posture of an Active Directory domain
external.license: Proprietary (free Basic edition, commercial licences).

why.text: PingCastle is closed-source .NET software and cannot be redistributed by Shadow OS.

how.text: Download the official release from PingCastle and run it on Windows or under Mono/.NET.

external.name: BloodHound.py
external.summary: Python data collector (ingestor) for BloodHound
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: The BloodHound.py ingestor is on PyPI/GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install bloodhound').

external.name: Social-Engineer Toolkit (SET)
external.summary: Framework for social-engineering attack simulations
external.license: TrustedSec SET licence (source-available); not in Debian.

why.text: SET ships under TrustedSec's own licence and depends on Metasploit, and is not in Debian.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run setup.py per the SET documentation; it expects Metasploit to be present.

external.name: Gophish
external.summary: Open-source phishing campaign framework
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Gophish is a Go application distributed as release archives outside Debian.

how.text: Download the official release archive for Linux and run the gophish binary.

external.name: King Phisher
external.summary: Phishing campaign toolkit with a graphical client
external.license: BSD-3-Clause (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: King Phisher is a client/server Python application on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install from the official repository using its documented install script.

external.name: Evilginx
external.summary: Man-in-the-middle framework for phishing with session capture
external.license: BSD-3-Clause (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Evilginx is a Go application distributed as release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the official release for Linux, or build with Go per the Evilginx documentation.

external.name: Modlishka
external.summary: Reverse-proxy framework for phishing and 2FA bypass research
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Modlishka is a Go application distributed as release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture, or build with 'go install' (Go is in Debian).

external.name: BeEF
external.summary: Browser Exploitation Framework for client-side assessment
external.license: MIT-like (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: BeEF is a Ruby application distributed on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run ./install then ./beef; Ruby is in Debian.

external.name: airgeddon
external.summary: Menu-driven multi-use wireless auditing script
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: airgeddon is a large Bash script on GitHub and is not in Debian; it drives the aircrack-ng suite (in Debian).

how.text: Clone the official repository and run ./airgeddon.sh; it uses tools such as aircrack-ng and hostapd.

external.name: Wifiphisher
external.summary: Rogue-AP framework for Wi-Fi phishing assessments
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: Wifiphisher is a Python tool on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run 'python setup.py install'; it needs a capable wireless adapter.

external.name: Fern Wifi Cracker
external.summary: GUI wireless security auditing tool
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: Fern Wifi Cracker is a Python/Qt GUI on GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run it per its docs; it wraps the aircrack-ng suite.

external.name: Kismet
external.summary: Wireless network and device detector, sniffer and IDS
external.license: GPL-2.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: Kismet is distributed via the project's own APT repository and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Add the official Kismet APT repository and install it per the Kismet documentation.
